policy.closure_rule: A regression is closed only when the fix and a permanent machine-enforced guard both exist.

regressions.example: Extension::$version referenced while canonical field is active_version
User security view accessed two_factor_secret on a model that had not retrieved the attribute
Spatie Activitylog v5 required attribute_changes but adapted migration omitted it
Focused Feature test inherited 127.0.0.1/songchart instead of canonical PostgreSQL test authority
Canonical test database was correct but migrations had not run before focused tests
PrivilegedAuditTest left an enabled provider fixture for the subsequent full suite
PHP 8.5 Docker build recompiled DOM/curl/mbstring/xml and failed around Lexbor headers
PowerShell installer assumed php composer.phar although composer.phar was absent
PostgreSQL host/database/auth configuration diverged between development and tests
PHPStan/Larastan errors were first discovered by the target installer
Historical full-source candidates omitted dependency lockfiles and target had to resolve packages
Validation/authorization/queue concerns risked moving out of Laravel-native boundaries
verify-runtime-authority-closure.php retained the pre-clean-schema test:feature alias after database authority changed
Performance verifier assumed environment preflight must be release:verify[0] after lockfile authority was intentionally added before it
Composer/canonical wrapper was visible but the actual failing Pest assertion was not present in the supplied tail
PostgresFirstDatabaseAuthorityTest hard-coded the old test:postgres command after shared DB authority added --prepare-schema
v20 installer checked a packaged repository-contract-manifest before recompiling it from the exact target authority tree
v20.1 executable authority APIs omitted iterable value types and used redundant null-coalescing on a shaped array
v20.2 parsed only literal Blueprint column arguments, missing nullableMorphs-generated *_type columns and misclassifying SongChart batch_uuid as upstream-required
Installer/canonical/release layers independently repeated quality/test/build gates while AGENTS/CLAUDE/GEMINI duplicated workflow rules.
v21 reproducible-environment verifier still searched for composer release:verify after canonical ownership moved to composer canonical:verify
v21.1 local-data-safety verifier still required test-database:safety inside release:verify after release became an alias and safety moved to canonical before stage/postgres.
v21.2 stack verifier required AGENTS.md to duplicate STACK_OVERVIEW/CAPABILITY_OWNERSHIP after AI instructions were consolidated into one protocol authority.
v21.3 foundation closure required verify to directly contain quality/test/build after verify became a compatibility alias to stage:verify.
v21.4 preserved exact Pest failure output but printed it before DB diagnostics, so copied terminal tails could omit the actual failing test while retaining only database state.
v21.5 full PostgreSQL suite exposed ten Architecture assertions that still treated verify/release:verify as copied pipelines and referenced removed preflight_order.
Laragon and Docker were both described as local development owners, allowing host toolchain drift from canonical Docker.
v22 architecture safety test assumed every machine-readable repository contract remained schema_version 1 after runtime-environments legitimately advanced to schema_version 2.
Multiple compatibility aliases and historical release scripts exposed equivalent verification/release entrypoints and allowed active docs/tests to drift between them.
v23 runtime authority closure still required test:all after verification surface reduction removed that alias.
v23.1 Architecture test required package-verified-source.php to contain closure_ready even though canonical closure ownership belongs to verify-artifact-provenance.php.
Activitylog attribute_changes was once added by editing an already-applied historical create migration, allowing migrate:fresh to pass while existing databases remained unchanged.

v24 privileged audit verifier and Architecture test still required attribute_changes in the frozen Activitylog create migration after migration lifecycle authority moved that repair to a forward migration.
v24.1 froze historical migrations with raw SHA-256, so canonical Pint/line-ending normalization changed bytes without changing migration semantics and produced false immutability failures.
v24.2 froze historical migrations from a packaging-side full-source artifact instead of the exact v23.2 canonical target, causing Pulse migration fingerprint drift.

Authority changes repeatedly reached canonical verification with stale verifier/Architecture consumers because no executable graph required every verification consumer to route to exactly one semantic owner.
Role capability checks were duplicated across UserRole, User, AppServiceProvider Gates, privileged services and observability verifiers, allowing authorization semantics to drift.
v26 Laravel alignment still required a direct Gate::define('access-admin') literal after authorization moved to Capability::cases() + AuthorizationMatrix.
v26.1 identity conflict UI verification still required a direct Gate::define(manage-identity-conflicts) literal after authorization moved to Capability + AuthorizationMatrix.

v26.2 removed User::isAdmin() from the packaged authorization refactor but the exact target still contained orphan app/Http/Middleware/EnsureUserIsAdmin.php, so PHPStan found a consumer absent from the packaging-side source reconstruction.
Controllers or read-model support classes may bypass the application boundary by directly opening transactions, mutating Eloquent models, or accumulating unclassified persistence queries.
A historical Identity Conflict Review UI task had already occupied STAGE_16_7_* paths; reusing the same filenames for Application Data Boundary would overwrite historical verification evidence.
